acts: RFC 9700, Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security

en.title: OAuth 2.1 draft: §4.1.3 rejects every token request without a code challenge, so, read literally, the PKCE exemption of §7.5.1.1 has no successful outcome
en.summary: §7.5.1.1 lets a confidential client that uses the OpenID Connect nonce skip the code challenge. The last bullet of §4.1.3 says the authorization server must reject a token request when the authorization request had no code challenge. Read literally, a client that uses the exemption receives a code but its token request must be rejected. RFC 9700 rejects only a token request that contains a code verifier, and the third bullet of §4.1.3 already covers that case. Draft-17 of 31 October 2026 rewords the bullet; the point is the same.
en.impact: Read literally, a confidential OpenID Connect client with nonce and without PKCE gets an authorization code whose token request must be rejected.
en.correction: Delete the last bullet of §4.1.3; the third bullet already covers a code verifier sent without a code challenge.
